title: DOW-UAP-D093, Analysis of Flying Object Incidents in the United States, 1948
doc_notes: This is a declassified Air Intelligence Division study (Study No. 203) from 1948 analyzing UAP incidents, and it contains detailed summaries of multiple close-approach encounters.

encounters.summary: Two Weather Bureau employees observed a metallic disk through a theodolite on three occasions at 15,000 and 27,000 feet.
encounters.entity_appearance: metallic disk, ellipse with flat bottom and round top

encounters.summary: An Air Force lieutenant reported seeing five or six white circular objects in close formation while flying at 10,000 feet.
Pilot and co-pilot of a DC-3 reported a flying disk larger than their aircraft crossing their path at 1,000 feet.
National Guard pilot reported a metallic object of tremendous size directly ahead before crashing.
Three balloon observers reported a round, indistinct object executing violent maneuvers at high speed.
encounters.location_name: Hollman Air Force Base, New Mexico

encounters.summary: Pilot of a P-51 pursued an intermittent white light that performed evasive maneuvers.
encounters.entity_appearance: small round ball of clear white light, 6-8 inches in diameter
encounters.entity_behavior: evasive, out-turned, out-speeded, and out-climbed the P-51

encounters.summary: Three reserve pilots encountered an unidentifiable flying object that performed vertical climbs and circled their aircraft.
encounters.entity_appearance: oblong ball with one light, dull gray glow, no wings, no exhaust
encounters.entity_behavior: climbed vertically, dropped below aircraft, circled, tight turn
